benefit.name: Assured Income for the Severely Handicapped (AISH)
benefit.amount: Monthly living allowance + health and personal benefits
benefit.summary: Alberta disability income assistance for people whose permanent disability prevents employment.
benefit.note: AISH is for a severe, permanent disability that prevents employment. Alberta now uses one application to assess both AISH and ADAP — submit it once, not separately for each program.
benefit.applyText: Apply for Alberta disability income assistance

detail.about: AISH is Alberta disability income assistance for adults whose severe, permanent disability prevents employment. It includes a monthly living allowance and may include health and personal benefits.
steps: Use Alberta's combined AISH/ADAP application — it assesses which program fits; you do not make two separate applications.
Complete your part and arrange the required medical report with a medical professional registered in Alberta.
Submit online, or use the application options Alberta Supports provides if online is not workable for you.
documents: Medical report showing how a severe, permanent impairment prevents employment
Proof of Alberta residency + Canadian citizenship / PR
Disability Income Assistance (DIA) application form, if you cannot apply online
Disability Assistance Medical Report, completed by your health professional
tips: The medical form should focus on how your condition permanently prevents employment, not just the diagnosis.
The combined application assesses AISH and ADAP. Alberta, not this tool, decides the program and benefit amount.
Use Alberta's AISH/ADAP benefit estimator for a household-specific estimate before relying on any amount.

If you receive AISH or ADAP, report the outcome of your CDB and/or DTC application to Alberta, including the approved CDB amount or a denial. Alberta says that when no CDB decision had been made by February 28, 2026, $200 was reduced from April 2026 benefits.
Getting help with the online application: phone the Alberta Supports Contact Centre at 1-877-644-9992, or 780-644-9992 in Edmonton.

Your health professional may charge you a fee to complete the Disability Assistance Medical Report, and you are responsible for paying it. If you are on Income Support that cost may be covered — ask your Income Support worker. For AISH clients who transitioned to ADAP and later choose to be assessed for AISH, Alberta says it will cover the cost of one Disability Income Assistance Medical Report; this support is not time-limited.
Benefits are backdated to the month AISH or ADAP received all of the information needed to approve your application, so sending every document sooner can mean an earlier start date for your benefits.
To check where your application is, phone 587-759-6810 in the Edmonton area, or 1-877-759-6810 toll free within Alberta.

If you leave AISH or ADAP, your file may be reopened quickly if it has been less than 2 years since you got your last AISH benefits and you did not leave AISH or ADAP due to a change in your medical condition. Contact AISH or ADAP if this applies to you; if not, you will need to reapply.
detail.time: Ask Alberta Supports for the current processing time.
detail.phone: DIA Application Processing Centre (applications and status): 1-877-759-6810

values.note: monthly living allowance plus health and personal benefits

extra.confirm: a severe disability that permanently prevents employment, AND income and assets under the AISH limits
extra.taxNote: AISH is not taxable. Other income and assets can affect assistance. If you receive AISH or ADAP, Alberta requires you to report the outcome of your Canada Disability Benefit and/or Disability Tax Credit application, including the approved CDB amount or a denial.
denials: The condition wasn't shown to be permanent, or was expected to improve with treatment.
The medical didn't show that the disability permanently prevents employment.
Income or assets over the limit.
The financial assessment did not meet the program rules.
extra.appeal: Read Alberta's current decision and appeal information before acting; rules and routes can change during the AISH/ADAP transition.

faqs.q: Do I apply separately for ADAP?
faqs.a: No. Alberta's current application assesses both AISH and ADAP and places eligible applicants in the program that fits.

faqs.q: Do I need the DTC first?
faqs.a: No, AISH is separate — but the DTC, CPP-D and RDSP are all worth applying for too.
It depends on Alberta's current rules and your household. Use the official AISH/ADAP benefit estimator rather than relying on a general figure.
